about: Stand-ins that `imitor init` proposes per package. kind: sqljs, skia or inert (a built-in stand-in), or none (the package's own web build works in `expo export --platform web`). Every entry was checked against the installed package at the version in `checked`: does it ship a .web.js entry, a plain file next to .native.js / .ios.js / .android.js files, a `browser` field, and does it load its native module at import time. Add an entry only after checking a real install.

expo-sqlite.why: Its web build runs wa-sqlite in a Worker loaded from the page's URL and needs SharedArrayBuffer (cross-origin isolation headers) for the synchronous API; a static export has neither.

@shopify/react-native-skia.why: Its web build draws through CanvasKit, which must be loaded (LoadSkiaWeb) before the app imports Skia; without it, Skia is built from an undefined global.

@bacons/apple-targets.why: iOS-only, but ExtensionStorage falls back to no-op functions when the native module is absent.

@posthog/react-native-plugin.why: Uses NativeModules when present and a no-op Proxy otherwise.

@react-native-async-storage/async-storag.why: Ships a web implementation (AsyncStorage.js next to AsyncStorage.native.js) backed by localStorage.

@react-native-community/datetimepicker.why: Its plain datetimepicker.js renders nothing and warns on web; it does not throw. Screens with a picker show no picker.

@react-native-google-signin/google-signi.why: Ships .web.js files for the button and the sign-in module.

@sentry/react-native.why: Ships .web.js files and runs on web.

expo-apple-authentication.why: Loads its native module with requireOptionalNativeModule and only creates the native button view on iOS.

expo-dev-client.why: Re-exports expo-dev-menu, which has a web build.

expo-localization.why: Its plain ExpoLocalization.js (next to the .native.js one) is the web build.

expo-notifications.why: Ships .web.js modules and plain files next to its .native.js ones.

expo-splash-screen.why: Its plain index.js (next to index.native.js) is the web build.

expo-store-review.why: Its plain ExpoStoreReview.js (next to the .native.js one) is the web build.

posthog-react-native.why: Plain JavaScript client with a .web.js file for its one native-only part.

react-native-purchases.why: Has a `browser` field and switches to its browser module on web.

react-native-svg.why: Ships .web.js files and draws real SVG.

react-native-webview.why: Its plain WebView.js renders a 'does not support this platform' message on web instead of throwing. The web page inside is not shown.
